method: own scripted + random rollouts only via nes_core.Pool / NESEnvironment (no external RAM maps / disassembly). Full 2KB CPU RAM ($0000-$07FF) scanned, not just zero-page.

step1_capture.boot_sequence: NOOP x120, SELECT x6, NOOP x20, START x8, NOOP x1000 (config-documented Mode-A 1P Mission-1 boot; the generic capture_start_state.py masher does not work on this title screen).
step1_capture.controllability_test: save_state at post-boot frame; RIGHT-vs-LEFT RAM diff over 90 steps.

player_x_0x5A_alone_REJECTED.reason: SATURATION (Kirby-lesson camera-clamp pattern): climbs 72->232-254 under hold-right then CAPS at each enemy gate (locked screen) regardless of continued forward input; a combat-biased probe showed 0x5A oscillating 232<->254 for hundreds of steps at a gate before any wrap.

room_counter_0xB2_discovery.method: diffed FULL RAM at the exact frame player_x wraps from near-max (232-254) down to a low value (0-72), filtered to events where health/lives are UNCHANGED (i.e. a real forward screen transition, not a death) -- 3-worker combat-biased rollout, 9000 steps.
room_counter_0xB2_discovery.coupling_rate: 2/3 events show a clean +1 step in lockstep with the px wrap; 1/3 shows +2 (attributed to frame_skip=4 aliasing collapsing a short room into one grouped step). No competing frame-counter address matched this pattern (the naive whole-RAM wrap-partner scan on the pure hold-right-only probe was dominated by high-churn free-running timers at 0x705/0x706/0x715/0x716/0x718/0x738/0xE3/0xE4 -- all REJECTED: churn ~1000/1k steps even under pure NOOP, the exact $001C-class trap).
room_counter_0xB2_discovery.death_regression_note: 0xB2 legitimately DROPS toward 0 on death/respawn (own probe: health 51->0 death frame shows 0xB2 2->0). This is a real attempt-reset, not a progress-signal defect; handled by the lives-decrement death check.

saturation_test.method: 3-worker, 180s checkpoint-and-retry random probe: each worker keeps its best (room, x) checkpoint and restores it on death instead of restarting cold -- no hand-authored route, pure right/attack-biased random sampling.
saturation_test.verdict: PASS -- 0xB2 climbed steadily to 15-16 with NO ceiling in sight in just 3 minutes of undirected play (vs. player_x alone, which caps every single screen at ~232-254). 0x62 (the other +1-at-transition candidate) plateaued at 1-2 and is REJECTED as the hi byte -- it does not accumulate.

wrap_test_gameplay_locked.noop_flat: 0x005A and 0x00B2 both static under pure NOOP from the start state (no free-running drift).
wrap_test_gameplay_locked.reversible: 0x005A falls under hold-LEFT (net -X vs hold-RIGHT net +X from the same root).

rejected_scroll_bytes.0x03B0_scroll_fine: churns 210/1k steps even before the player moves (own NOOP-adjacent probe) -- 'jitters under lock' per the existing ram_mapping comment; no clean wrap-partner in the full-RAM scan.
rejected_scroll_bytes.0x03B2_scroll_coarse: mono=1.0 on a coarse per-step diff stat but the raw sampled series is NON-monotonic (16,16,32,32,96,48,160,176,96,32,240,48,...) -- camera/parallax jitter that only LOOKS monotone under the wraparound-correction stat, not a real position counter. NOTE: this is a DIFFERENT address from the 0x00B2 room counter chosen above; do not confuse the two.

y_z_depth.rationale: This is a 2.5D beat-'em-up: UP/DOWN move the player along the street's DEPTH axis (per the profile's own action_space comments), which is the correct analog of platformer 'y' here, not a jump-height byte.

noop_flat.verdict: PASS -- dead flat over 200 NOOP steps

hold_up_200.verdict: rises to a hard lane ceiling (96)

hold_down_200.verdict: falls to a hard lane floor (48)

tests.verdict: PASS -- flat under NOOP, reversible, bounded by the street width (a real depth-lane position, not a camera artifact)

y_z_depth.true_jump_ballistic_search: Searched for a classic platformer dip-then-return signature under the A+B 'jump' input (profile's action_space comment). None found clean within the probe window: candidates 0x005B/0x0037F/0x0037E moved under repeated A+B holds but did NOT return to baseline after release (monotone drift, not a ballistic arc) -- consistent with A+B triggering a directional lunge/kick animation rather than a vertical hop. Not used; the Z-depth axis (0x0072) is the game's real vertical-equivalent dimension and is what the action_space exposes as controllable 'vertical' movement.

lives.test: 3-worker combat rollout: sequence 2->1->0->255 observed (255 = the documented GAME OVER wraparound). is_dead fires on the FIRST decrement (2->1), well before any lineage could reach the 255 wrap, so the wraparound is a non-issue for the solver in practice.

health.test: 64 at start; decreases in combat (including under pure NOOP once enemies reach the player); hits exactly 0 at death and resets to 64 on respawn. Not used directly by the solve: block (lives decrement is the death signal) but corroborates every death event used above.

mission.note: Rock-stable at 1 throughout Mission 1 across all probes (including through deaths); its increment on a real mission clear could not be produced by a scripted/random bot (matches the config's pre-existing documentation). level_key left [] (coverage baseline) per task guidance.

step4_smoke.command: in-process make_game(profile) + nes_core.Pool(num_workers=3) loading the captured start state on all 3 workers

result.rollout: 400 steps of right+B mash across all 3 workers (deterministic, no restarts)
result.verdict: PASS -- make_game builds GenericGame, Pool loads the start state and steps cleanly, cell_fn returns a sane 5-tuple, and progress climbed 72 -> 4072 (room 0 -> room 15) from pure scripted play with zero restarts.

max_progress_reached.note: max_gx_in_max_area (the solver's own live telemetry) plateaued at 4072 from the FIRST 60s checkpoint through the full 6 minutes -- a hard combat gate at room 15/16 that the default hyperparameters (burst=64, sticky=0.5, deep-bias=0.4) did not break through in this budget. cells kept growing throughout (805 -> 2103), i.e. the archive kept finding NEW diverse states below the frontier even while the frontier itself was pinned.

out_travels_random.method: A matched-budget (108491 steps/worker, 3 workers -- identical total step count to the go_explore run) PURE RANDOM baseline: uniform action sampling, restore the single best (progress) checkpoint on death (no archive, no cell selection, no directed bias). Own script, own rollout, same start state / same profile.
out_travels_random.verdict: HONEST NEGATIVE RESULT: in this bounded 6-minute / ~325k-step budget, Go-Explore did NOT out-travel the matched-budget random-restart baseline on raw frontier distance -- random (greedy single-checkpoint restore) reached room 16 (progress 4328) vs. Go-Explore's room 15 (progress 4072), a difference of about one room. This is plausible for a game whose bottleneck is a single combat gate with little need for backtracking: a greedy hill-climb spends 100% of its step budget pushing the ONE current-best checkpoint forward, while Go-Explore's archive deliberately spends budget returning to and diversifying EARLIER cells (2103 distinct cells cataloged, vs. zero for the random baseline, which keeps no archive at all). That breadth is Go-Explore's actual product for the downstream BC/DAgger distillation step (many diverse states to learn from, not just one lucky line) -- it is just not reflected in a bare max-progress number over a short run. Reported honestly per task instructions rather than reframed as a win; a longer budget and/or a higher deep-bias/lower burst may change this.

step6_observatory.interpretation: ALL top-10 predicates gate on the 'jump' (A+B) probe -- corroborating step2's own finding that A+B's effect on position is CONDITIONAL on some player-state/action-mode byte (0x0003, 0x0028, 0x0009, 0x002B/0x002C look like a correlated family of animation/action-state bytes; 0x0503/0x0416/0x03F5-6 are candidate secondary mode flags). This matches the 'true_jump_ballistic_search' rejection in step2: A+B is a context-sensitive attack/lunge, not a free hop, and these bytes are the gating condition. Good candidates for a future state_sig: entry if the archive stalls on an attack-timing gate.
